# Expected Shortfall / CVaR (historical, 95%) (`expected_shortfall_historical_95`)

*Category: Tail behavior · Nature: estimated · Unit: decimal_return · Formula id: `expected_shortfall_historical_95@v1` · Methodology 0.1.0*

## 1. What does it measure?

Average return in the periods at or below the 95% VaR threshold.

## 2. Formula

```text
mean(r_t | r_t <= Q_0.05(r))
```

## 3. Required inputs

Periodic simple returns.

## 4. Is higher or lower better?

Higher is better.

## 5. Plain-language interpretation

When things went badly (the worst 5% of periods), this was the average return.

## 6. Professional interpretation

Historical Expected Shortfall (CVaR); a coherent risk measure (Acerbi & Tasche, 2002) that accounts for the severity of tail losses.

## 7. Assumptions

- The supplied history is representative of the tail.

## 8. When can it be misleading?

- Few observations fall in the 5% tail: with monthly data a 95% estimate rests on roughly n/20 points.
- The history does not contain a stress period.
- Returns are smoothed, which compresses the tail.

## 9. Minimum sensible data

At least 2 observations; low confidence when fewer than 5 observations are expected in the tail (n < 100). (policy `tail`: Requires at least 2 observations; low confidence when fewer than 5 observations are expected in the 5% tail (n < 100), moderate when fewer than 10 (n < 200).)

## 10. Reference implementations

| Library | Function | Agrees | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| PerformanceAnalytics 2.0.4 (R) | `ES(p=0.95, method='historical')` | yes | Uses returns strictly below the quantile; identical unless an observation equals the quantile exactly. |
| QuantStats 0.0.81 | `stats.cvar` | no (documented difference) | QuantStats conditions on a parametric VaR threshold. |
| empyrical-reloaded 0.5.12 | `conditional_value_at_risk` | yes | Uses returns at or below the 5th percentile. |

## 11. Sources

- Acerbi, C., & Tasche, D. (2002). On the Coherence of Expected Shortfall. Journal of Banking & Finance, 26(7), 1487-1503.
- Jorion, P. (2006). Value at Risk (3rd ed.). McGraw-Hill.
- Bacon, C. R. (2021). Practical Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement (2nd ed.). Wiley.

## 12. OpenFactsheet convention

Mean of returns at or below the linear-interpolated 5% quantile; signed.
